headline: This 2020 law requires certain foreign companies that sell securities in the U.S. to certify government ownership status and face trading bans if U.S. auditors cannot inspect their accounting firms.
what_it_does: The law applies to issuers of securities whose audit reports are prepared by a foreign accounting firm that the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board cannot inspect. Such issuers must certify that they are not owned or controlled by a foreign government. If the board cannot inspect the firm for three consecutive years, the issuer's securities are banned from trading on a national exchange or through other methods. Affected foreign issuers must also disclose, for each non-inspection year, the share of stock held by government entities, whether those entities have a controlling financial interest, whether any board members are officials of the Chinese Communist Party, and whether the company's articles of incorporation contain any Chinese Communist Party charter.

who_it_affects.group: Foreign companies that sell securities in the United States
who_it_affects.how: They must make government-ownership certifications and make annual disclosures if their audit firm cannot be inspected by the board.

who_it_affects.group: Foreign companies whose audit firms cannot be inspected for three years in a row
who_it_affects.how: Their securities can be banned from trading on U.S. national exchanges or through other methods.

who_it_affects.group: Foreign accounting firms that audit U.S.-listed companies
who_it_affects.how: Their clients may face disclosure and trading consequences if the board cannot inspect the firm.
They would no longer be able to trade the securities of companies covered by a three-year trading ban.

who_it_affects.group: Investors who hold shares of affected foreign companies
who_it_affects.how: They could lose the ability to trade those shares on U.S. exchanges if a trading ban takes effect.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on December 18, 2020, and the official summary does not state a separate effective date for these requirements.
